title: Zimbabwe Rhodesia
capsule: Zimbabwe Rhodesia was an unrecognized state that existed from 1 June to 12 December 1979, created when Prime Minister Ian Smith's Rhodesia conducted an internal settlement with moderate black leaders—including Bishop Abel Muzorewa, who became the first black prime minister. The compromise was rejected internationally because it excluded the major liberation movements ZANU and ZAPU and failed to satisfy the conditions of UN Security Council resolutions. The Lancaster House Agreement negotiated in London ended the Zimbabwe Rhodesia experiment: a British-supervised ceasefire was followed by elections in February 1980 that brought Robert Mugabe's ZANU-PF to power, and the country became Zimbabwe on 18 April 1980.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political and territorial history of Zimbabwe Rhodesia is well documented; the to-date of 1983 in the dataset likely reflects a data-model artifact rather than a factual boundary.
